rules.statement: A vested interest is an assured and certain right, as opposed to a contingent or conditional one.
rules.supporting_quote: "When the word 'vested' is used in this sense, Austin (Jurisprudence vol. 2, lect. 53) points out that in reality -a right of one class is not being distinguished from a right of another class but that a right is being distinguished from a chance or possibility of aright"
